Hi Stephanie / David —

Thanks for the conversation last week. We're preparing our FY28 budget and need to finalize the contract terms for our Redwood renewal. Our usage continues to be spiky (marketing events + batch indexing windows) so we're focused on two items:

1) Commit pacing: we want a model that lets us ramp committed tokens across the year rather than a single up-front commit. Ideally quarterly rebalances.
2) Fall-through credits: we need some protection for months where we consistently under-run the committed tier so those dollars don't go to waste (or at least convert to credits against next quarter).

Attached is a high-level usage snapshot for Q2 and a draft SOW with projected traffic. Can you confirm whether Redwood can do a paced-commit with rolling credits, and roughly what a committed discount might look like (vs. our current PAYGO run rate)?

Also, procurement asks whether invoice timing can align to our fiscal quarter (we run PO approval on quarter boundaries). If you can provide a sample billing cadence + an operational playbook for how credits flow, that will help accelerate sign-off.

Short meeting this week would be great — we can do Wed/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks,

Hi Eva —

Really helpful context and thanks for the usage snapshot. We can definitely support a paced-commit approach. Quick outline of three pragmatic options that have worked for similar customers:

• Option A — Retainer conversion: convert a portion of expected PAYGO spend into a 12-month retainer at a fixed committed rate; quarterly top-ups allowed. Biggest discount but less flexible.

• Option B — Commit pacing w/ quarterly rebalances: commit to a target annual volume but allow quarterly reallocation; unused quota up to a capped amount (e.g., 20% per quarter) becomes fall-through credits applied to next quarter. Mid-sized discount + operational flexibility.

• Option C — Price-hold + usage credits staircase: keep PAYGO pricing but lock current price for 12 months (price-hold) and tier in credits as usage thresholds are hit — lower near-term risk for you, smaller discount.

Operational notes: we can align invoice timing to your fiscal quarters (send invoices on the first business day of the quarter; net-60 by request) and provide a short playbook for credit application. SLA crediting is standard (service outages only, capped) but we can discuss an uplift for enterprise SLA in the contract.

If you like Option B (sounds like it matches your ask), we can propose:
• 12-month term with annual committed volume baseline
• Quarterly rebalances with a 20% fall-through credit cap per quarter
• 12% committed discount vs current PAYGO effective rates
• One-time onboarding credit of $12,500 to offset migration/implementation tasks

Propose a 30-minute sync Wed 17 Aug 9:30–10:00 PT or Thu 18 Aug 9:30–10:00 PT. If you confirm, I'll pull together a short term sheet and a sample invoice cadence for procurement.

—

Eva —

Thanks for confirming. Per internal review here is the operational and commercial proposal we can commit to for the term sheet: 

Commercials (Option B, commit pacing):
• Term: 12 months; customer commits to an annual baseline volume (we'll seed with your expected annual token volume).
• Quarterly rebalances permitted (no penalty) to shift committed volume between quarters.
• Fall-through credits: unused committed tokens up to 20% of the quarter are converted to applied credits to the next quarter at full committed unit value. Credits cannot be refunded for cash.
• Discount bands on committed units: 12% discount at baseline, 15% discount if annual committed volume >= baseline + 20%, 18% discount if annual committed volume >= baseline + 40%.
• Onboarding credit: $12,500 applied on first invoice.

Operational notes:
• Invoice cadence: invoices issued on the first business day of each fiscal quarter (we will include PO reference lines and accept PO numbers for your AP team). Standard payment terms net-60 (we can do net-45 if procurement needs faster clearance).
• Credits playbook: we'll issue a credits statement at quarter close and apply credits to the first invoice of the following quarter. Monica will manage the ledger and provide a monthly credits report.
• SLA credits remain limited to service-level breaches; incidental compensation is handled case-by-case.

Next steps: if this looks acceptable I'll send a 1-page term sheet and the HubSpot deal will be updated (BR-2027-0841). Once you confirm committed baseline and target uplift band (e.g., +20% or +40%), David and I will finalize pricing and route the DocuSign.

Proposed immediate ask from you: reply with the committed baseline you want us to seed (we can use the Q2 average extrapolated) and which uplift band you want to target.

If you'd rather walk through live, Thu 18 Aug 16:00–16:30 PT works for our team — otherwise we can finalize asynchronously.
